title: Smooth morphisms are universally locally acyclic
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $f$ is universally locally acyclic [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf]: for every scheme morphism $S'\to S$, every geometric point $\bar x'$ of $X'=X\times_S S'$, and every positive integer $n$ prime to its residue characteristic, the base-change morphism $X'\to S'$ is locally acyclic at $\bar x'$ relative to $\underline{\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z}$. In particular $f$ itself is locally acyclic. Neither properness nor a bound on the relative dimension is assumed.

proof.text: Smoothness is stable under arbitrary base change, so it suffices to establish local acyclicity for a smooth f. Fix x and an admissible positive integer n. Its image in the residue field at x is a unit: use characteristic zero or Bezout for coprimality with the characteristic. The residue embedding carries this unit to the geometric field Omega.

source.place: Tag 0GJQ, proposition-smooth-locally-acyclic; Tags 0EZU, 03QO and 0GJR for the comparisons

proof.text: Put s=f x and A=S_(s). The chosen strict-local ring is local and strictly henselian. Its canonical evaluation into Omega factors as its surjection onto the relative separable closure followed by the field embedding. The surjection is local, as is the field embedding, so evaluation reflects units. Since n is a unit in Omega, n is a unit in A and in its global sections. Form Xprime=X times_S A and lift x using the canonical closed-point lift of s.

source.place: Tag 0GJQ, proposition-smooth-locally-acyclic; Tags 0EZU, 03QO and 0GJR for the comparisons

proof.text: Apply strictBaseClosedPointLocalizations to this cartesian square and the pointed strict-local maps. It gives an isomorphism from the strict localization of the image of xprime to A, an isomorphism on the source strict localizations, and compatible isomorphisms of every vanishing-cycle fibre. In particular every original test point is transported by the inverse base isomorphism; no algebraicity restriction is imposed.

proof.text: On the strict-local base A apply smooth base change to the map Spec K to A and the constant group M=ULift(Z/n). Both schemes are affine, so that map is qcqs; n is invertible on A, and constant geometric stalks are M, killed by n. Regard the abelian sheaf as a sheaf of ULift Z-modules via the existing coefficient-forgetting equivalence. The derived coefficient-forgetting comparison and its single-functor comparison transport the smooth exchange isomorphism back to abelian sheaves. Apply the strict-local exchange criterion at xprime, using Spec.preimage of its canonical strict-local map, to obtain the bijective cohomology pullback from A_(fprime xprime) times_A Spec K to Xprime_(xprime) times_A Spec K.

source.place: Tag 0GJQ, proposition-smooth-locally-acyclic; Tags 0EZU, 03QO and 0GJR for the comparisons

proof.text: A separably closed field is strictly henselian: its residue map is a ring isomorphism. Its constant-section unit is invertible, by the sheafification unit at the terminal object and uniqueness of right adjoints; all positive derived cohomology vanishes. Transfer these properties first along the isomorphism from A_(fprime xprime) times_A Spec K to Spec K, then along the bijective comparison of the preceding step, and finally along the fibre isomorphism of step 3. In degree zero use bijective_cohomologyMap_zero_iff and the constant-sheaf adjunction identity that pullback sends each constant section to itself. In positive degrees use the natural Ext/derived-cohomology comparison, bijectivity, and the inverse-image constant-sheaf isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0GJQ, proposition-smooth-locally-acyclic; Tags 0EZU, 03QO and 0GJR for the comparisons

proof.text: The germ-compatible strict-local constant comparison identifies the actual canonical alpha with the constant-section unit followed by global sections of its coefficient isomorphism. The constant geometric stalk is M. Naturality of the constant-section unit transports its invertibility along that stalk isomorphism, and functoriality transports positive cohomology vanishing. Thus the canonical alpha is invertible and every required positive cohomology object vanishes. This proves local acyclicity; step 1 supplies universality.
